sources.entry: C#: _Loading and rendering 3D skeletal animations from scratch in C# and GLSL_

summary.title: Skeletal Animation (Loading and rendering 3D skeletal animations from scratch in C# and GLSL)
summary.one_liner: You learn the 3D graphics math (vectors, matrices, transforms, projections, quaternions) and the engine structure (textures, assets, world objects) needed to load and render skeletal animations in C# with OpenTK.
takeaways: Vertices bundle position, texture coordinates and normals, and are uploaded to the GPU via OpenGL for rendering.
A model matrix is built from translation, scale and rotation, and the final screen position is found by multiplying projection, view and model matrices.
Multiplication order matters: translating then rotating gives a different result from rotating then translating.
Textures are loaded as bitmaps, uploaded with GL.TexImage2D, and mipmaps are generated for smaller renders.
An asset system with importers keyed by file extension and a cache lets models, animations and textures load by name.
summary.summary: The page is a hands-on project write-up, implemented in C# with the OpenTK library and GLSL shaders, that explains how 3D models and skeletal animations are stored and drawn. It walks through vector and matrix operations with short code examples and printed results, covering translation, scaling, rotation, reflection, orthographic and perspective projection, and quaternions. It then describes the engine structure: vertices, the model/view/projection pipeline, a WorldObject class that caches transforms, pose and animation selection, texture loading into OpenGL, and a generic asset importer and cache. The article is cut off partway through the texture class, and the id Tech 4 (md5mesh/md5anim) importer is listed in the topics but not covered in the visible text.
